questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'AUGMENT'.
questions.explanation: 'Augment' means to make something greater in size or amount, i.e. to increase. 'Reduce' is its opposite, meaning to make smaller. 'Delay' means to postpone, and 'ignore' means to disregard, neither of which relates to increasing, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to 'HOSTILE'.
questions.explanation: 'Hostile' means unfriendly or antagonistic; its opposite is 'friendly'. 'Aggressive', 'angry' and 'unkind' are all close in meaning to hostile, expressing conflict or ill will, so none of them is the antonym and each is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about nouns:

(i) An abstract noun can always be seen and touched.
(ii) A common noun names a general item.
(iii) A proper noun begins with a capital letter.
(iv) A collective noun names a group of things.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: A common noun names a general item, a proper noun is capitalised, and a collective noun names a group, so (ii), (iii) and (iv) are correct. Statement (i) is false because an abstract noun names an idea or quality that cannot be seen or touched; hence any option containing (i) is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The sentence 'She sings good' is grammatically incorrect.
Reason (R): The verb 'sings' needs the adverb 'well', not the adjective 'good', to describe it.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both are true and R explains A: 'sings' is a verb and must be modified by the adverb 'well', so 'sings good' is wrong precisely for that reason. Hence 'Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)'. The second is wrong because R does explain A, and the third and fourth wrongly deny a true statement.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: The old scholar refused to part __________ his rare collection of books. __________
questions.explanation: The phrase 'part with' means to give up possession of something, so 'part with his books' is correct. 'from' pairs with 'part from' meaning to separate from a person, not an object. 'of' and 'to' do not collocate with 'part' in this sense, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are abstract nouns?

(i) Honesty
(ii) Table
(iii) Courage
(iv) Freedom

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Honesty, courage and freedom are qualities or ideas that cannot be physically touched, so they are abstract nouns and (i), (iii) and (iv) are correct. 'Table' (ii) is a concrete noun naming a physical object; hence any option containing (ii) is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following idioms with their meanings:

Column I:
(a) To bury the hatchet
(b) To have cold feet
(c) To read between the lines
(d) To throw in the towel

Column II:
(i) To become nervous before an event
(ii) To make peace after a quarrel
(iii) To give up
(iv) To understand a hidden meaning

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: 'Bury the hatchet' = make peace, 'have cold feet' = become nervous, 'read between the lines' = grasp a hidden meaning, and 'throw in the towel' = give up — matching '(a)-(ii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iii), (d)-(iv)'. The second swaps (a) and (b), the third swaps (c) and (d), and the fourth wrongly links 'bury the hatchet' with hidden meaning, so those are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'ADEPT'.
questions.explanation: 'Adept' means highly skilled or proficient at something. 'Clumsy' means awkward, its opposite. 'Slow' refers to lack of speed, and 'weak' refers to lack of strength, neither of which conveys skill, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about tenses:

(i) 'They have been playing' is in the present perfect continuous tense.
(ii) 'She had left' is in the past perfect tense.
(iii) 'We are going' is in the simple present tense.
(iv) 'He will have finished' is in the future perfect tense.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: 'Have been playing' is present perfect continuous, 'had left' is past perfect, and 'will have finished' is future perfect, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. Statement (iii) is false because 'We are going' is present continuous, not simple present; hence any option containing (iii) is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to 'COMMENCE'.
questions.explanation: 'Commence' means to begin; its opposite is 'conclude', meaning to end. 'Begin', 'start' and 'initiate' are all synonyms of commence, expressing the idea of starting, so none of them is the antonym and each is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct article to complete the sentence: __________ Himalayas form the northern boundary of India.
questions.explanation: Names of mountain ranges take the definite article 'the', so 'The Himalayas' is correct. 'A' and 'an' are indefinite articles used for singular, non-specific nouns and cannot precede a plural range name. 'No article' is wrong because ranges require 'the', so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: What does the idiom 'a bolt from the blue' mean?
options: A flash of lightning in a storm
questions.explanation: 'A bolt from the blue' means something that happens suddenly and unexpectedly. 'A flash of lightning' reads the phrase too literally. 'A clever idea' and 'a long-awaited piece of news' do not capture the sense of a sudden shock, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank with the correct homophone: The athlete injured his __________ while landing awkwardly after the jump. __________
questions.explanation: 'Heel' is the back part of the foot, which fits an injury while landing. 'Heal' is a verb meaning to make well again. 'Hill' is a small elevation of land, and 'heap' means a pile, neither of which fits the context of a foot injury, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the phrase 'a good advice', the article 'a' is used incorrectly.
Reason (R): 'Advice' is an uncountable noun and does not take the article 'a'.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both are true and R explains A: 'advice' is uncountable, so it cannot take 'a'; one says 'a piece of advice' instead, which is exactly why 'a good advice' is wrong. Hence 'Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)'. The second is wrong because R does explain A, and the third and fourth wrongly deny a true statement.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct preposition: The suspect could not account __________ his movements on the night of the crime.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'account for' means to explain or give a reason, so 'account for his movements' is correct. 'to' collocates with 'answer to', 'of' does not pair with 'account' here, and 'with' fits 'deal with', so those prepositions are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following sentences are grammatically correct?

(i) Each of the boys was present.
(ii) Neither of them is coming.
(iii) One of my friends is a doctor.
(iv) The news are very good today.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: 'Each', 'neither' and 'one of' take singular verbs, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. Statement (iv) is wrong because 'news' is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb ('The news is good'); hence any option containing (iv) is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about parts of speech:

(i) 'Under' is a conjunction.
(ii) 'Beautifully' is an adverb.
(iii) 'Happiness' is an abstract noun.
(iv) 'Swim' can be used as a verb.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: 'Beautifully' is an adverb, 'happiness' is an abstract noun, and 'swim' can act as a verb, so (ii), (iii) and (iv) are correct. Statement (i) is false because 'under' is a preposition (or sometimes an adverb), not a conjunction; hence any option containing (i) is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'VIGILANT'.
questions.explanation: 'Vigilant' means keeping careful watch for danger, i.e. watchful. 'Careless' means inattentive, its opposite. 'Sleepy' and 'idle' both suggest a lack of alertness, so none of them matches the meaning of vigilant and each is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following verbs with the prepositions that correctly follow them:

Column I:
(a) abstain ______
(b) confide ______
(c) comply ______
(d) vouch ______

Column II:
(i) in
(ii) from
(iii) for
(iv) with

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The correct collocations are 'abstain from', 'confide in', 'comply with' and 'vouch for', matching '(a)-(i), (b)-(ii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(iii)'. The second wrongly gives 'abstain in', the third wrongly gives 'comply for', and the fourth wrongly gives 'abstain with', so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to 'RIGID'.
questions.explanation: 'Rigid' means stiff and unable to bend; its opposite is 'flexible', meaning able to bend or adapt. 'Stiff', 'hard' and 'firm' are all close in meaning to rigid, so none of them is the antonym and each is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct homophone to complete the sentence: For dessert, the chef prepared a light and airy chocolate __________.
questions.explanation: 'Mousse' is a light, whipped dessert, which fits the sentence. 'Moose' is a large deer-like animal, 'mouse' is a small rodent (or a computer device), and 'moss' is a small green plant, none of which is a dessert, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about punctuation:

(i) A full stop ends a declarative sentence.
(ii) A colon is used to end a question.
(iii) An exclamation mark shows strong feeling.
(iv) A comma is used to separate items in a list.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: A full stop ends a statement, an exclamation mark shows strong feeling, and a comma separates list items, so (i), (iii) and (iv) are correct. Statement (ii) is false because a question ends with a question mark, not a colon; a colon introduces a list or explanation, so options with (ii) are wrong.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: What does the idiom 'to steal the show' mean?
options: To attract the most attention and praise
questions.correctAnswer: To attract the most attention and praise
questions.explanation: 'To steal the show' means to draw the most attention and outshine others at an event. 'To leave a performance early' and 'to cancel an event' are unrelated, and 'to take something without paying' reads 'steal' too literally, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: Despite mounting pressure, the officer refused to yield __________ the unlawful demands. __________
questions.explanation: The verb 'yield' collocates with 'to' when it means to give in, so 'yield to the demands' is correct. 'on' pairs with 'rely on', 'for' with 'wait for', and 'at' with 'aim at', none of which fits 'yield', so those prepositions are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The sentence 'He is more taller than his brother' is incorrect.
Reason (R): 'Taller' is already a comparative form, so 'more' should not be used with it.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both are true and R explains A: 'taller' is already comparative, so adding 'more' creates a double comparative, which is exactly why the sentence is wrong. Hence 'Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)'. The second is wrong because R does explain A, and the third and fourth wrongly deny a true statement.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'EMINENT'.
questions.explanation: 'Eminent' means well known and respected, i.e. famous or distinguished. 'Unknown' and 'ordinary' suggest the opposite, lacking distinction. 'Humble' means modest, which is unrelated to fame, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following words can function as both a noun and a verb?

(i) Run
(ii) Book
(iii) Quickly
(iv) Water

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: 'Run', 'book' and 'water' can each act as a noun and a verb (e.g. a run/to run, a book/to book, the water/to water), so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. 'Quickly' (iii) is only an adverb; hence any option containing (iii) is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following homophones with their meanings:

Column I:
(a) Fair
(b) Fare
(c) Coarse
(d) Course

Column II:
(i) The money paid for a journey
(ii) Just, or light in colour
(iii) A series of lessons or a direction
(iv) Rough in texture

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: 'Fair' means just or light-coloured, 'fare' is the money paid for travel, 'coarse' means rough, and 'course' is a series of lessons or a direction — matching '(a)-(i), (b)-(ii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(iii)'. The second swaps fair and fare, the third swaps coarse and course, and the fourth wrongly labels fair as rough, so those are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about clauses and phrases:

(i) A main clause can stand alone as a sentence.
(ii) A subordinate clause cannot stand alone.
(iii) A relative clause usually begins with a relative pronoun.
(iv) Every phrase contains a subject and a finite verb.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: A main clause stands alone, a subordinate clause cannot, and a relative clause begins with a relative pronoun, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. Statement (iv) is false because a phrase does not contain a subject and finite verb (that defines a clause); hence any option containing (iv) is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to 'DEFICIT'.
questions.explanation: 'Deficit' means a shortfall, especially when spending exceeds income; its opposite is 'surplus', meaning an excess. 'Shortage', 'loss' and 'debt' are all close in meaning to deficit, expressing lack, so none of them is the antonym and each is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct preposition: The new building does not conform __________ the safety regulations.
questions.explanation: The verb 'conform' collocates with 'to', so 'conform to the regulations' is correct. 'with' pairs with 'comply with', 'for' with 'apply for', and 'in' with 'believe in', none of which fits 'conform', so those prepositions are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct preposition: The brave constable was commended __________ his prompt action during the emergency.
questions.explanation: The verb 'commend' collocates with 'for', so 'commended for his action' is correct. 'on' pairs with 'congratulate on', 'with' with 'provide with', and 'of' with 'accuse of', none of which fits 'commend', so those prepositions are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank to complete the idiom: After his release from prison, he decided to turn over a new __________ and lead an honest life. __________
questions.explanation: The idiom 'to turn over a new leaf' means to make a fresh start, so 'leaf' completes it correctly. 'Page', 'chapter' and 'day' may seem related to a fresh start, but they are not the words used in this fixed idiom, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'HAZARDOUS'.
questions.explanation: 'Hazardous' means risky or dangerous. 'Safe', 'harmless' and 'secure' all suggest the absence of danger, which is the opposite of hazardous, so none of them is a synonym and each is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about subject-verb agreement:

(i) 'Each of the answers are correct.' is correct.
(ii) 'A number of students were absent today.' is correct.
(iii) 'The number of students is fifty.' is correct.
(iv) 'Bread and butter is a wholesome breakfast.' is correct.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: 'A number of' takes a plural verb, 'the number of' takes a singular verb, and 'bread and butter' as a single dish takes a singular verb, so (ii), (iii) and (iv) are correct. Statement (i) is false because 'each of' requires a singular verb ('is correct'), not 'are'; hence any option containing (i) is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The sentence 'Ram is taller than any other boy in the class' is correct.
Reason (R): The phrase 'any other' wrongly excludes Ram from the comparison.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.explanation: A is correct: 'taller than any other boy' is the proper way to compare Ram with the rest of the class. R is false because 'any other' is exactly what correctly excludes Ram himself from the comparison, which is required, not a mistake. So '(A) is correct but (R) is not correct' is right; the first and second wrongly accept R, and the fourth wrongly rejects A.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct homophone to complete the sentence: The ship sailed smoothly across the calm __________.
questions.explanation: 'Sea' is a large body of salt water, which fits a ship sailing across it. 'See' is a verb meaning to perceive with the eyes, 'seas' is the plural but does not fit 'the calm ___' as a singular, and 'cee' is not a standard word, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following sentences are correctly punctuated?

(i) It's a lovely day today.
(ii) The dog wagged it's tail.
(iii) Who's coming to the party?
(iv) The books on the shelf are theirs.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Sentences (i), (iii) and (iv) use the apostrophe correctly: 'It's' means 'it is', 'Who's' means 'who is', and 'theirs' is a possessive with no apostrophe. Sentence (ii) is wrong because the possessive should be 'its tail', not 'it's tail'; hence any option containing (ii) is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to 'PROSPERITY'.
questions.explanation: 'Prosperity' means a state of flourishing and wealth; its opposite is 'poverty', the state of being poor. 'Wealth', 'success' and 'growth' are all close in meaning to prosperity, so none of them is the antonym and each is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following words with their synonyms:

Column I:
(a) Brave
(b) Wise
(c) Rapid
(d) Huge

Column II:
(i) Swift
(ii) Courageous
(iii) Enormous
(iv) Sagacious

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: 'Brave' means courageous, 'wise' means sagacious, 'rapid' means swift, and 'huge' means enormous — matching '(a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii)'. The second swaps brave and wise, the third swaps rapid and huge, and the fourth wrongly links brave with swift, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: What does the idiom 'to make ends meet' mean?
options: To finish a task on time
To manage within a limited budget
To reach the end of a journey
questions.correctAnswer: To manage within a limited budget
questions.explanation: 'To make ends meet' means to manage one's expenses within a limited income. 'To finish a task on time' relates to deadlines, 'to bring two people together' is about relationships, and 'to reach the end of a journey' is literal travel, none of which matches the financial sense, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about voice:

(i) 'The cake was eaten quickly' is in the passive voice.
(ii) 'She writes poems' is in the active voice.
(iii) 'He runs very fast' is in the passive voice.
(iv) 'The bridge is being built' is in the passive voice.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) and (iv) have the subject receiving the action with 'be' plus a past participle, so they are passive, and (ii) is active because the subject performs the action, making (i), (ii) and (iv) correct. Statement (iii) is false because 'He runs very fast' is active, not passive; hence options with (iii) are wrong.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct preposition: The chairman decided to dispense __________ the usual formalities and begin at once.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'dispense with' means to do without something, so 'dispense with the formalities' is correct. 'of' pairs with 'approve of', 'from' with 'refrain from', and 'for' with 'wait for', none of which fits 'dispense' in this sense, so those prepositions are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank with the correct homophone: The teacher asked the student to read the poem __________ so that everyone could hear. __________
questions.explanation: 'Aloud' means in a voice that can be heard, which fits reading so everyone can hear. 'Allowed' is the past tense of 'allow', meaning permitted, a different word. 'Alowd' and 'alloud' are misspellings that do not exist in standard English, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are pairs of synonyms?

(i) Happy - Joyful
(ii) Big - Large
(iii) Fast - Quick
(iv) Hot - Cold

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Happy/Joyful, Big/Large and Fast/Quick are pairs with similar meanings, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are synonyms. Pair (iv) is wrong because 'hot' and 'cold' are antonyms, having opposite meanings; hence any option containing (iv) is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The plural of the animal name 'mouse' is 'mouses'.
Reason (R): Some English nouns form their plurals in an irregular way.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: A is false because the plural of the animal 'mouse' is the irregular form 'mice', not 'mouses'. R is true, as many English nouns do have irregular plurals. So '(A) is not correct but (R) is correct' is right. The first and second wrongly treat A as correct, and the third wrongly calls R incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: What does the idiom 'to cross swords' with someone mean?
options: To travel a long distance together
questions.explanation: 'To cross swords' with someone means to argue or come into conflict with them. 'To become close friends' is nearly the opposite, 'to make a solemn promise' relates to commitment, and 'to travel together' is literal and unrelated, so those options are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to 'SUPERIOR'.
questions.explanation: 'Superior' means higher in rank or quality; its opposite is 'inferior', meaning lower. 'Higher', 'greater' and 'better' are all close in meaning to superior, so none of them is the antonym and each is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about articles:

(i) 'A' and 'an' are definite articles.
(ii) 'A' is used before a word beginning with a consonant sound.
(iii) 'An' is used before a word beginning with a vowel sound.
(iv) 'The' is a definite article.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: 'A' precedes consonant sounds, 'an' precedes vowel sounds, and 'the' is the definite article, so (ii), (iii) and (iv) are correct. Statement (i) is false because 'a' and 'an' are indefinite articles, not definite ones; hence any option containing (i) is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following idioms with their meanings:

Column I:
(a) A white elephant
(b) To jump on the bandwagon
(c) To play second fiddle
(d) A wolf in sheep's clothing

Column II:
(i) To join a popular trend
(ii) A costly but useless possession
(iii) A dangerous person who appears harmless
(iv) To take a less important role

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: 'A white elephant' = a costly useless possession, 'jump on the bandwagon' = join a popular trend, 'play second fiddle' = take a lesser role, and 'a wolf in sheep's clothing' = a dangerous person who seems harmless — matching '(a)-(i), (b)-(ii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(iii)'. The other options wrongly swap these meanings, so they are incorrect.
